edis-memory-system v3.2.3 
 What's New in v3.2.3
1. Semantic Tag System (LLM-Generated)
Every hourly sync now generates 5 concept-level tags per session via LLM, stored as Redis Set inverted indices. This replaces vector DB dependency with a zero-dependency lightweight alternative.
2. New Commands: tag & search
memory.sh tag <user> <date> — View tags for a specific date    — memory.sh search <user> <tag1> [tag2 ...] — Intersection-based multi-tag lookup across dates    Both commands pull from clean, automatically maintained tag indices.
3. Full Chain Verified
Single-tag lookup, multi-tag intersection (AND), combined tag+summary queries — all tested and passing in production.
4. Product Philosophy Locked
Lightweight. Zero burden. Config-driven. Serving individual developers — not enterprise complexity. No vector DB, no external dependencies beyond Redis.
v3.2.3 completes the semantic layer without adding a single pound of weight. The system remains: 1 config file, 1 script, Redis.

Major Release — Complete Architecture Refactoring
v3.2 is not a minor patch. It's a ground-up redesign of the entire memory synchronization system.
What changed:
- 6 scripts consolidated into a single `memory.sh` — sync / get / set / heartbeat / stats all in one place
- Configuration-driven: all usernames managed via `/etc/memory-users.conf`, no code changes needed to add users
- `sync` command outputs structured JSON; the cron LLM only handles summarization decisions, no more shell output parsing
- Self-reference filter: cron sessions no longer pollute their own memory data
- Per-user distributed locks enabling parallel sync for multiple users
Upgrading from v3.1? The old scripts (redis_memory.sh, cron_heartbeat_ping.sh, etc.) are deprecated. Everything is now managed by `memory.sh`. Clean up old files before installation.

redis-memory-system v3.1.1 Changelog
2026-05-25

Core Architecture Changes
Merged exec calls

File search + conversation extraction + Redis deduplication combined into a single script.

Eliminates variable loss across processes caused by the three independent exec steps in v3.1.

Atomic Redis writes

Replaces three separate redis-cli calls with a Lua EVAL script.

HSET + EXPIRE + SET last_seen completed in one transaction.

Prevents data inconsistency if a crash occurs midway.

Distributed lock

SET NX EX 600 prevents two cron jobs from writing simultaneously.

trap cleanup EXIT ensures the lock is automatically released when the script exits.

Retry mechanism

When file reading fails, retry up to 2 times with a 1‑second interval.

Fixed Bugs
File selection: most matches → latest by modification time

Old bug: an old file from May 8th with 29 matches would override a new session from today with 28 matches, causing missed memories.

Fix: use ls -t to pick the most recently modified file.

Shell syntax errors do not abort the script

Old bug: when grep -c returned empty, shell would error with [: 0: integer expression expected.

Fix: proper handling of empty return values.

Threshold of 5 was too high

Old bug: short dialogs like “Are you there?” (only 2 user messages) were filtered out and never stored.

Fix: lowered threshold to 2.

Cron self‑reference filtering

Old bug: the cron prompt contained a user ID, so cron’s own session was also matched by grep.

Fix: head -10 checks if the file contains the [cron: prefix and skips self‑referencing files.

Script Improvements
All scripts now validate argument count and content to prevent ghost records from insufficient parameters.

redis_memory_user.sh username validation

At startup, checks whether USERNAME is still the placeholder "your_username" to prevent accidentally writing to memory:your_username.

cron_heartbeat_ping.sh externalised user list

Supports three configuration methods: environment variable REDIS_MEMORY_USERS, configuration file /etc/redis-memory-users.conf, or a hardcoded array.

New commands in redis_memory.sh

ping: check Redis connectivity.

stats: count memory days and characters per user.

New standalone script scripts/extract_dialog.py

Replaces the Python code previously embedded in the cron prompt for transcript conversation extraction.

Avoids shell quoting issues and makes it easier to cite in papers.

recent command upper limit of 30 days

Prevents accidentally traversing the entire history when a large number is passed.

Documentation Updates
SKILL.md and README.md completely rewritten:

Architecture diagram updated to reflect the actual v3.1.1 flow.

Deployment notes synchronised (timeout raised from 120 s to 180 s, tool restrictions set to exec,read).

Added a complete problem‑solution mapping table.

Known Limitations
Redis has no persistence configured (RDB/AOF). Restarting Redis loses the last 7 days of memories.

Tied to OpenClaw’s transcript file path; adapting to other platforms requires changes.

No quantitative evaluation metric for LLM summary deduplication.

1. Fully Automatic Sync
- v2.1: Agent Heartbeat-triggered writes, dependent on Session activity
- v3.1: OpenClaw Cron takes over, runs every hour automatically. Agent does nothing.
2. Bypassed dmScope Isolation
- v2.1: Heartbeat could only access the current Session's conversation. Writes skipped when Session was idle.
- v3.1: Cron reads Transcript JSONL directly via filesystem (tail -200), no longer blocked by API-level isolation.
3. Semantic Deduplication
- v2.1: No dedup — repeated triggers could write the same summary multiple times
- v3.1: Compares new summary with existing one before writing; skips if the same information is already captured.
4. Meta-Instruction Filtering
- v2.1: Summaries often contained debug text like "sleep", "retrigger", "poll"
- v3.1: Prompt explicitly filters out technical and meta-instruction content
5. Memory Space Isolation
- v2.1: Cron logs and heartbeats were written into the user's memory hash (141-entry pollution incident)
- v3.1: Introduced `cron:health` as an isolated key. System data never mixes with user memory.6. Tool Restriction
- v3.1 added `--tools exec,read,write,edit` to prevent recursive Cron execution or unintended API calls

- v2.1: Prompt was embedded in scripts, hard to maintain
- v3.1: Extracted into `openclaw_cron_prompt.txt` for independent editing

更新内容：

5️⃣ 保底Cron脚本 — 新增 cron_heartbeat_ping.sh，每小时执行：写活跃标记 + 升级 draft + 兜底报告。
📦 新增文件：cron_heartbeat_ping.sh、redis_memory_user.sh 🔄 更新文件：setup.sh、SKILL.md、README.md

🔧 Bug Fixes
Fix memory loss on session reset — Heartbeat was silently idling due to target:none config, never writing conversation summaries to Redis. Changed to target:last with a triple-layer write architecture; any single layer succeeding guarantees persistence.
Fix cron writing timestamps only — The system cron was only writing heartbeat pings every hour without promoting draft summaries to permanent storage. Rewritten to auto-detect draft:<user>:summary keys and upgrade them to memory:<user>:YYYY-MM-DD with 7-day TTL.
Fix complete memory loss after session recycling — OpenClaw's 4:00 AM reset, 120-minute idle reset, and 24-hour no-interaction recycle wiped all conversation history. Solved with a triple-layer architecture where each layer operates independently.
Fix cross-user data leakage risk — Shared scripts between different users could accidentally read each other's memory. Added redis_memory_isolated.sh for strict isolation with hard rules prohibiting cross-user access without explicit authorization.
⚡ Improvements
Triple-layer write architecture: Agent → draft key (12h TTL) → System Cron(hourly) + OpenClaw Cron(every 2h) + Heartbeat(every 2h) → Permanent storage(7 days)
Draft key bridge: draft:<user>:summary acts as an intermediate layer with 12-hour auto-expiry; zero garbage even if all cron jobs fail
Zero token cost: Entire pipeline runs on Redis + Shell scripts — no API tokens consumed
Multi-user isolation: Dual scripts + separate key namespaces; physical data separation between users; cross-user access requires explicit authorization
7-day auto-expiry: No manual cleanup needed; Redis TTL 604800s automatically evicts stale data

中文介绍：
🧠 Redis Memory System — 跨 Session 短期记忆，给 Agent 装上"短期记忆海马体"
OpenClaw Agent 每次会话被回收后（04:00框架重置 / 120分钟空闲 / 24小时平台超时），都会像失忆一样醒来。这套系统在会话之外增加了一层 Redis 存储，让 Agent 醒来第一时间知道你昨天聊了什么。
工作原理 每次对话结束时，Agent 自动将当日对话摘要写入 Redis Hash，KEY 级 TTL 设为 7 天。下次 Session 启动时，SOUL.md 铁律强制先查 Redis 再回话——从"我是谁"到"我们聊到哪了"，全程衔接。
核心特性
🔹 跨 session 记忆保持 — 不依赖框架层的上下文持久化，独立于 Session 生命周期
🔹 多账号数据隔离 — 同一进程服务多位用户时，memory:账号A 和 memory:账号B 是独立的 Hash key，双脚本+SOUL 铁律双重保障
🔹 Heartbeat 自动续写保底 — 即使对话意外中断（断网/崩溃/超时），下一次 Heartbeat Poll 会自动检查并写入摘要，零数据丢失
🔹 7 天 TTL 自动过期 — 短期记忆就该自动遗忘。不撑磁盘、不需维护、不留隐私隐患
🔹 双脚本设计 — 通用版 redismemory.sh 适合单用户/互信多用户场景；隔离版 redismemoryisolated.sh 通过 REDISMEMORY_USER 环境变量硬编码用户身份，防止跨账号误操作
🔹 参数强校验 — set -euo pipefail 保障脚本健壮性，日期格式与有效性双重校验（YYYY-MM-DD + date -d 验证），缺参友好提示
🔹 操作审计 — 独立的 actions:system Hash 记录下载文件、安装软件等后台操作，解决"谁干的"溯源问题
🔹 轻量极致 — 每条记忆仅 0.5~2KB，代理端无需额外依赖，只需 Redis-server 运行在 localhost:6379
与官方 MEMORY.md 的区别 官方 OpenClaw 提供文件式 MEMORY.md（长期）和 memory_search（语义检索），但依赖会话上下文写入。这套系统在文件层之外增加了一层 Redis——7天窗口内的记忆自动存活，不需要手动提炼。两套互补：Redis 管"短期不忘"，MEMORY.md 管"长期不朽"。
English Description:
🧠 Redis Memory System — Cross-session short-term memory for OpenClaw agents. Think of it as a hippocampus for your AI.
OpenClaw agents lose session context at predictable boundaries: daily framework reset (04:00), idle timeout (120 min), and platform-level disconnection (24h). Without external memory, every new session starts from scratch — the agent has no idea what you talked about yesterday. This system bridges that gap with a lightweight Redis layer that preserves daily conversation summaries across session boundaries.
How it works When a conversation ends, the agent automatically writes a daily summary to a Redis Hash keyed by user and date (memory:<user> → YYYY-MM-DD). Each key has a 7-day TTL. On every new session start, SOUL.md iron rules force the agent to query Redis before responding to the user — transforming "Who am I talking to?" into "We were discussing X yesterday, let's pick up from there."
Key Features
🔹 Cross-session persistence — Survives framework resets, idle timeouts, and platform disconnections. Independent of OpenClaw's session lifecycle
🔹 Multi-user isolation — memory:userA and memory:userB are separate Redis Hash keys within the same instance. Dual-script architecture + SOUL.md behavioral rules create defense in depth against data leakage
🔹 Heartbeat auto-save fallback — If a conversation cuts off unexpectedly (network drop, crash, timeout), the next Heartbeat poll automatically checks for unsaved context and writes it. Zero data loss by design
🔹 7-day TTL auto-expire — Short-term memory should forget by default. No disk bloat, no manual cleanup, no privacy residue
🔹 Dual scripts — redis_memory.sh (general purpose) for single-user or trusted multi-user scenarios; redis_memory_isolated.sh (sandboxed) enforces a fixed username via REDIS_MEMORY_USER environment variable, preventing accidental cross-user writes
🔹 Strict validation — set -euo pipefail for script-level robustness; dual-layer date validation (regex format check + date -d existence check); friendly error messages for missing arguments
🔹 Action audit trail — A separate actions:system Hash records system operations (file downloads, software installs), answering "Who did what and when?"
🔹 Extremely lightweight — ~0.5–2KB per memory entry. No agent-side dependencies beyond a running Redis-server on localhost:6379
vs. OpenClaw's built-in MEMORY.md OpenClaw's official memory system uses file-based MEMORY.md (long-term) and semantic search (memory_search/memory_get), but relies on in-session context for writes. This skill adds a Redis layer beneath it — day-level summaries survive automatically within the 7-day window without manual curation. The two complement each other: Redis handles "don't forget what we just talked about," MEMORY.md handles "remember this forever."
